chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, from Bashir, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, when the Muslim servant goes out from his house to visit his brother for the sake of Allah, not for anything else, seeking the Face of Allah with desire for what is with Him, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, assigns to him seventy thousand angels who call out to him from behind until he returns to his house: 'Indeed, you have done well, and Paradise is made better for you.'

key_terms.أَلَا طِبْتَ: Indeed, you have done well / Be pleased
key_terms.طَابَتْ لَكَ الْجَنَّةُ: Paradise is made better for you

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a brother for the sake of Allah?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize that ziyarat (visiting) is an act of worship when performed with pure intention (ikhlas). The presence of seventy thousand angels announcing 'Ala tib wa tabbat lakal jannah' underscores the immense spiritual status and divine favor bestowed upon the believer who strengthens brotherly ties for Allah's sake alone.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Khalid and Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Bin Imran Al Halby, from Bashir, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the Muslims servant goes out from his out to visit his brother for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, not for something else, seeking the Face of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> wishing regarding what is in His<sup>azwj</sup> Presence, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Allocate seventy thousand Angels calling out to him from behind him until he returns to his own house: ‘Indeed! You have done well, and the Paradise is (Made to be) better for you’’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya ibn ‘Imran al-Halabi from Bashir from abu Hamza from abu la’ far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“If a Muslim (believing) servant (of Allah) comes out of his house to visit his brother, due to Allah’s relation, not for any other reason and just because of Allah, with interest in what is with Allah, Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, appoints seventy thousand angels who applaud behind him until he comes home, ‘How beautiful is your deed! How beautiful is paradise for you!”’
